title: fix(core): the action runner admits mailto: through one navigation-target answer shared with resolveCtaHref (objectui#12191)
body:
Fixes #12191
Clause-②: yes (widening)

A `type: 'url'` action or an `element:button` whose target is `mailto:` published cleanly and then failed at click with "Invalid URL scheme". `ActionRunner.isValidUrl` admitted only `http(s)` and relative paths, while app-shell's `resolveCtaHref` already admitted `mailto:` through a scheme test of its own. This PR is the runner half of ruling A+ (comment 6121792024 on the card). The spec half is objectstack-ai/objectstack#23010; the ruling says the two halves do not block each other. First producer: cloud's `CONTACT_SALES_URL` (`mailto:sales@objectos.ai`) for objectstack-ai/cloud#2775.

## What changed

- **One answer, two callers.** `@object-ui/core` exports `classifyNavigationTarget(url)` and its `NavigationTargetKind` type, from the new module `packages/core/src/actions/navigationTarget.ts` through the actions barrel. It answers `'web'` (`http://`, `https://`), `'mail'` (`mailto:`), `'path'` (`/path`, `./path`) or `null` (refused). The admitted predicate is "not null"; the same call also answers "in place" (`'mail'`) and "absolute" (`'web'` or `'mail'`), which is what `resolveCtaHref` needs. The runner (`navigateTo` and `navigateOnSuccess`) and `resolveCtaHref` both import it. `isValidUrl` is deleted, and neither caller keeps a scheme list.
- **The admitted set is closed.** `javascript:`, `data:`, `tel:` (not admitted, per the ruling) and every other scheme answer `null`. So does a protocol-relative `//host`, together with the two spellings the browser's URL parser reads as `//host`: a backslash right after the first slash, and any target holding a tab, line feed or carriage return, which the parser deletes before it reads anything. Scheme names compare case-insensitively, as the parser compares them.
- **`mailto:` navigates in place.** In `navigateTo` (the `type: 'url'` action and its `navigation` alias) and in `navigateOnSuccess` (`onSuccess.navigate`), a `mailto:` target sets `window.location.href` and returns. It never opens a new tab, `openIn` is not consulted, and the host's navigation handler is not called (H4 says why). This is the same full-page mechanism the runner already uses for `/api/` targets.
- **The refusal names the set.** Both runner refusals now carry one sentence, the module constant `NAVIGATION_TARGET_REFUSAL`: "Invalid URL scheme. Only http://, https://, mailto: and in-app relative paths (/path, ./path) are allowed." It keeps the "Invalid URL" opening the existing `ActionRunner.test.ts` refusal cases assert.
- **app-shell.** `resolveCtaHref` maps `'web'` to as-is plus a new tab and `'mail'` to as-is in place, which were its answers before. Every other target takes the control-plane-relative branch, as before.

## Behaviour changes beyond `mailto:` (please read)

1. **`//host` is now refused by the runner.** Before, `isValidUrl` admitted it because it starts with `/`, and the runner handed it to the navigation handler as an in-app path (`external: false`). The ruling lists `//evil.example/x` among the refused targets.
2. **Upper-case schemes are admitted.** The runner now admits `HTTP://…` and `HTTPS://…` as external URLs and `MAILTO:…` as a mail target; it refused them before. The CTA's http test was already case-insensitive, and one shared answer had to pick one rule; the case-insensitive rule keeps `resolveCtaHref`'s http(s) answers unchanged. The runner's external test now reads the same answer, so an upper-case http URL reaches the handler as external, not as a route. `resolveCtaHref` now also passes `MAILTO:…` through as-is.
3. **An html-tier anchor whose href resolves to a path starting with `//`** (for example an authored `.//x`) is now refused by the runner instead of routed. `toInternalPath` in `html-elements.tsx` already treats `//` as external; only a dot-segment spelling reaches the runner this way.

## Measurements (the dispatch's H1 to H6)

### H1: every caller, classified against the fork clause

The classifier's callers after this PR, all user-click navigations:

| Caller | Reached from | Navigation sinks |
|---|---|---|
| `ActionRunner.navigateTo` | `executeUrl` (`type: 'url'`), `executeNavigation` (the `navigation` alias), so every `element:button` action with `actionType: 'url'` or a `to` / `navigate` target (`ElementButtonRenderer` calls `useAction().execute`), and the html-tier anchor's internal-link click (`runner.execute` with `type: 'url'`) | `window.location.href` (the `/api/` case, and now `mailto:`), the host navigation handler, `window.open` (no handler, new tab), `result.redirect` (no handler; the html-tier anchor follows it with `window.location.assign`) |
| `ActionRunner.navigateOnSuccess` | `onSuccess.navigate` after the `api` / `script` action the user clicked succeeds | handler, `window.open`, `result.redirect`, and now `window.location.href` for `mailto:` |
| `resolveCtaHref` | `CtaButton`'s anchor `href` in `EnvironmentEntitlementDialog` | the browser's own anchor click |

`element:button` measured: `ElementButtonRenderer` (`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/elements.tsx`) builds the action and passes it to `useAction().execute`, so a url target goes through the runner (`executeUrl` to `navigateTo`), not a separate renderer path.

No caller is an iframe `src`, a fetch target or a server-side redirect, so the fork clause does not trigger. Read and left alone because they are not callers: the console `apiHandler`'s absolute-target test in `useConsoleActionRuntime` and the runner's `executeAPI` build fetch targets and never consulted `isValidUrl`. `executeActionSchema` copies `action.redirect` into `result.redirect` without any scheme check (see Acceptance notes).

### H2: `resolveCtaHref`

Before: `/^https?:\/\//i` or `startsWith('mailto:')` passed the URL through as-is (new tab for http(s), in place for `mailto:`). Everything else was prefixed with `apiBase`. Now `'web'` and `'mail'` give the same two answers, and everything else takes the same prefix branch. Today `javascript:alert(1)` is prefixed like a relative path: `https://cp.examplejavascript:alert(1)` with a base, and a bare `javascript:alert(1)` href with an empty base (prod). This PR leaves that unchanged: the shared answer is `null` for it, so it is never passed as absolute. A pin asserts that for `javascript:`, `data:`, `//host` and `tel:`.

### H3: where the symbol lives

`@object-ui/app-shell`'s `package.json` declares `"@object-ui/core": "workspace:*"`, and app-shell already imports core symbols (`ExpressionEvaluator`, `resolveViewId` and others). Core's package entry re-exports `./actions/index.js`, so the classifier sits beside the runner and app-shell imports it from `@object-ui/core`. The single-definition pin walks every non-test source under `packages/*/src`. It asserts that exactly one file binds `classifyNavigationTarget`, that the dialog imports it from `@object-ui/core` and that the runner imports it from `./navigationTarget.js`. It also asserts that neither of those two files holds a scheme test in code, with comments blanked by `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`. A CONTROL row proves the scheme-test pattern matches the definition it guards.

### H4: in place, and `openIn`

- Before: `navigateTo` read `openIn` first: `'new-tab'` gave a new tab, `'self'` gave the same tab, and any other value fell back to `source.newTab ?? isExternal`. `'new_window'` and `_blank` are not `openIn` members, so they took that fallback. A `mailto:` target never got that far, because it was refused.
- Now: `mailto:` returns before `openIn` is read. It is pinned with `openIn: 'new-tab'`, with the legacy `navigate.newTab: true`, with `onSuccess.openIn: 'newTab'`, and through a real `element:button` with `openIn: 'new-tab'`. In every case it sets `window.location.href` once, the handler is not called and `window.open` is not called.
- Why not the host handler: the console's `navigateHandler` (`useConsoleActionRuntime`) calls `window.open(url, '_blank', …)` whenever `external || newTab`, and `navigate(url)` otherwise. Measured with the installed react-router-dom 7.18.2: `resolvePath('mailto:a@b.com', '/apps/crm/account')` answers pathname `/apps/crm/account/mailto:a@b.com`. Handing `mailto:` to the handler therefore either opens a tab or routes it under the current page.
- `utils/appRoute.ts` (`resolveNotificationTarget`) is not on this path: its callers are the inbox popover and the arrival notifier. It already classes any scheme, `mailto:` included, as external.

### H5: where the message lives

The message was a core string literal in `navigateTo`, with a second spelling in `navigateOnSuccess`'s `console.warn`. No i18n key holds it: a tree-wide `git grep` for the literal hits only `ActionRunner.ts`. Both now read one module constant, so no locale pack changed.

### H6: other URL readers (read, not changed)

- `components` `html-elements.tsx` `sanitizeHref`: a deny-list (`javascript|data|vbscript:`), so a raw anchor keeps `mailto:` and also `tel:`. `toInternalPath` sends only scheme-less paths to the runner. **Differs:** deny-list rather than a closed set, and admits `tel:`.
- `fields` `UrlField.tsx` (readonly): links only `http://` / `https://` (case-sensitive) in a new tab, and renders any other value, `mailto:` included, as plain text. **Differs:** narrower.
- `app-shell` `utils/appRoute.ts` `resolveNotificationTarget`: any scheme or `//` is external and the caller opens it; everything else is an in-app route. **Admits `mailto:`** as external.

## Tests

All at `6edd9b1` (this branch's head), unless marked otherwise.

- **New pins:**
  - `packages/core/src/actions/__tests__/navigationTarget.mailto-12191.test.ts`: the classifier table; `mailto:` in place on `url`, the `navigation` alias, legacy `newTab`, no handler and `onSuccess.navigate`; the refused set, each with the message that names `http://`, `https://`, `mailto:`, `/path` and `./path` and not `tel:`; the CONTROL rows `https://…`, `/path` and `./path`, handed to the handler exactly as before.
  - `packages/app-shell/src/environment/__tests__/resolveCtaHref.sharedTarget-12191.test.tsx`: the single definition, and the CTA agreeing with the shared answer.
  - `packages/components/src/__tests__/element-button-mailto-12191.test.tsx`: the real `element:button` through the real runner.
- **Whole core package:** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/core/` gave `Test Files 200 passed (200)`, `Tests 3987 passed | 27 skipped (4014)`.
- **Every test that reads an edited file by path or imports its symbols:** the three new pins, the `element:button` / html-anchor / action-forward suites, `packages/app-shell/src/environment/__tests__/`, the plugin-detail result-dialog suites, `FormPage.recordId`, `toast-demo-dispatch-6250`, and the `scripts/__tests__` suites for one-authority-per-exported-name, side-effects consistency, unit-registry-absence-collision, shared-global-leak-guard and action-forward-parity. Result: `Test Files 26 passed (26)`, `Tests 424 passed (424)`.
- **Reverse verification, at `fc703bf`** (the runner and dialog have not changed since): `ActionRunner.ts` and `EnvironmentEntitlementDialog.tsx` were checked out from the base commit, landing confirmed by blob hash (`6fe3e6a0…` and `33acbdda…`), and `isValidUrl` was back (count 3). The three new pin files then gave `Tests 23 failed | 33 passed (56)`, the expected direction (red). The restore leg checked both files out from `HEAD`, confirmed the blobs (`1c0fd241…`, `b7d4e0b3…`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. What stayed green under ablation were the controls and the module-level rows: the classifier tables, the http(s) and path controls, the CTA's web and lower-case mail rows, and the single-definition population.
- **Type-check:** `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) for `@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/components` and `@object-ui/app-shell` printed `Done` for each, exit 0, after the turbo builds of `@object-ui/core...` and of `core^...`, `app-shell^...`, `components^...` (28 tasks, all successful). Each package's `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*.test.ts(x)`, and the components one caught a typing slip in the new pin before `0df0c68` repaired it.
- **Gates, all exit 0:**
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers` (`OK`)
  - `check:test-path-roots` (`OK`)
  - `check-changeset-presence` (`7 source file(s) of 3 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`)
  - `check:changeset-claims` (`No pending changeset names a file this change touches`)
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals` (`No test source names a pending changeset`)
  - `check:control-bytes` (`OK`)
  - `check:new-line-citations` (`VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0`)
- **Lint, narrowed and proven:** `pnpm exec eslint --format json` over the 7 changed `.ts` / `.tsx` files: 7 files, 0 errors, 13 warnings. All 13 were already on the base commit, measured on the base blobs: 12 `no-explicit-any` in `ActionRunner.ts` and 1 `react-refresh/only-export-components` in the dialog. The new files have 0. Why the narrowing excludes nothing:
  1. The population comes from `eslint.config.js`, whose `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` holds all 7.
  2. The count, 7, is read from the JSON output.
  3. The config has no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), its plugins are `@eslint/js`, react-hooks, react-refresh, typescript-eslint and the local `eslint-rules`, and no local rule reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot move any verdict on an untouched file.
- **NOT MEASURED, left to CI:**
  - The whole `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/components` suites. This is a declared narrowing: the dispatch asked for targeted runs, and every test that reads the edited files ran above.
  - `pnpm lint` over the tree.
  - The console eager-closure budget, which needs a console build (Bundle Analysis).

## Acceptance notes

- **`resolveCtaHref`'s refused branch is unchanged** (H2). With an empty `apiBase`, a served `javascript:` CTA URL still reaches the anchor's `href`. The installed React 19.2.8 blocks a `javascript:` href at render, but the package's React peer range also admits 18. The URL comes from the control plane's `upgrade_url` / `contact_url`, and no producer of a script URL there was found. Not filed; carrier: none.
- **`executeActionSchema`'s `result.redirect` is not scheme-checked.** The only in-tree reader of a runner `result.redirect` is the html-tier anchor, and only for `type: 'url'` actions, which go through `navigateTo`. So nothing navigates it today. Not filed; carrier: none.
- **`onSuccess.navigate` with `mailto:` runs after an API response.** A browser may require recent user activation to launch an external protocol handler, so a slow response could fall outside that window. Not measured in a browser.
- **Docs:** no page under `content/docs` and no package README names the url action's admitted schemes (searched for `mailto`, `javascript:` and scheme wording), so none became false. A page saying it is outside this claim's file surface.
- **Changeset:** `@object-ui/core` is `minor` (an added export) and `@object-ui/app-shell` is `patch`. `@object-ui/components` gets only a test file.
